content.title: 'Temptation Island' season 2: Who stayed together and who broke up?
content.text: Temptation Island, which Entertainment Weekly once called "the world's most ill-advised form of couples therapy," is back with a new season. The long-running series is enjoying its latest act on Netflix after previously airing on Fox and USA, tantalizing viewers by thrusting four couples due for a reckoning into an exotic locale overflowing with sultry singles whose only goal is to flirt. The point is to put the relationships to the test — if their love can survive this, it can survive anything, right? Season 2 of the Netflix iteration dropped all nine of its episodes on April 10, with early promises to stay faithful evaporating as new attractions emerged and simmering resentments boiled over. The final bonfire is a bloodbath. Below, we detail where each couple stands following the finale. Who stays together? Who calls it quits? And who drops the l-word to a single they met in the villa? Read on for the answers. Scarlett and Cole Scarlett Bentley and Cole Mueller on 'Temptation Island'. Netflix Status: No longer together Scarlett and Cole came into the season on different pages. They left it that way, too. While he was confident in their union, she felt a lack of communication. She was also nursing trust issues, making Cole determined to stay faithful to her throughout the season. He was successful in that regard, even as she forged an emotional connection with Bradley, someone she connected with early in the process. During the final bonfire, he reveals that he felt betrayed by her spending so much time with Bradley. Prior to coming on the show, they promised each other they wouldn't go on multiple dates with a single tempter. He called his experience on the show "traumatizing." Still, he claims he grew throughout the experience, and promises that he'll never lie to her again. As evidence of this, he confesses to her that he read her private journal when the men went to the women's villa. The old Cole, he says, would never confess to such a breach of privacy, but Scarlett is unmoved, believing he's only doing it for the cameras. She doesn't think he's grown at all, nor does she believe him when he discusses "emotional connections." "Do you know what emotional connections are?" she asks. "When I speak of depth, do you understand what that looks like? I just wonder if we even speak the same language." In the end, Cole chooses to leave the island with her. Scarlett, on the other hand, wants to leave alone. "There's no way things would be drastically different," she says of their relationship. "I have to choose myself now." Cole accepts this, but we later see him angrily slamming a water bottle against the seat on the car ride away from the villa. "There's a deeper issue with her, man," he says. "It's something that I can't fix." Sydney and Mikey Sydney McGregor and Mikey Bivens on 'Temptation Island'. Netflix Status: No longer together Sydney and Mikey seemed doomed from very early in the process. During the first bonfire, Sydney is shown a clip of Mikey saying he hopes to "shoot his shot" with one of the singles, India. Mikey never ended up doing anything beyond flirting, but his unfortunate turn of phrase was all Sydney needed to begin exploring her options in the villa. She soon formed a connection with the handsome, musically-inclined Xzavier. The pair shared a kiss and a deep emotional bond, something that didn't go unnoticed by Mikey. "I've been miserable as hell in there," he says at the final bonfire, thunder crashing in the distance. "I had to watch you fall in love with someone every single day." Sydney is unrepentant, though, and tells Mikey that she can't shake the unfaithful person he was when they were in college. "The person you were is still repeating in my head," she says. Her resentment runs deep. "I started to realize that I was making myself smaller in our relationship so you could shine," she adds. "You loved the idea of me, but you never really loved me." Mikey claims he's grown and that he's left the old version of himself behind. Still, he can recognize that there's no hope for their relationship moving forward. Host Mark L. Walberg chimes in, bringing Mikey to tears by saying he "grew into a man" over the course of the season. Mikey chooses to leave the island alone. Sydney, meanwhile, wants to continue exploring her connection to Xzavier. After Mikey leaves and Xzavier joins her, she confesses that she's fallen in love with him. "I've been loving you for some time, Sydney," he replies, agreeing to leave with her. "You make it really easy." Shyanne and Jack Shyanne Blankenship and Jack Mason on 'Temptation Island'. Netflix Status: No longer together Bitterness abounds during Shyanne and Jack's final bonfire, though that's not too surprising considering both of them ventured into the Temptation Haven with some of the singles. Jack seems resigned as he tells her how the process helped him realize how "stuck" they were after five years together, repeating the same "toxic cycle" over and over. Shyanne is more direct — and much angrier. "I don't think you thought about me through this experience one time," she says, adding that she'd begun anticipating heartbreak well before filming began. "You made me look like a fool." They're both grateful for their experience on the show. He discovered that he doesn't need to be scared of being alone. She found her confidence again, and feels renewed. "You don't deserve any part of the new version of me," she tells him. Unsurprisingly, they both leave the island alone. Probably a good thing. Kaylee and Summit Summit Wallace and Kaylee Needham on 'Temptation Island'. Netflix Status: Still together Oh, thank goodness, a happy ending. Kaylee and Summit's history is littered with commitment issues, break-ups, and make-ups, and those old wounds remain evident during the final bonfire. She tells him that he often makes her feel unworthy of his love. "I want to feel like I am the prize, loved for every piece of me, without having to ask for it," she says. Summit, who remained faithful to her throughout the season, is receptive, but also stung by remarks he saw her making about him in a clip at an earlier bonfire. While recalling a time in which she was crying and he left her alone to hang out with his friends, she called him a "sociopath." She admits to saying that out of anger, assuring him that she doesn't think he's a sociopath. He replies by saying that, as much as it hurt him, "the message I received is to show more empathy." From there, he acknowledges his previous shortcomings and gives her the support she's been craving from him. "You are enough," he says. "You are everything that any guy on the planet would want, and you shouldn't change for anyone because you are enough." She's stunned by these words coming out of his mouth, and even more shocked when he declares wholeheartedly that he wants to fully commit to their relationship. To back it up, he pulls out a dog collar with a key on it. The collar represents their mutual desire to care for a pup together, while the key is his way of asking if she'd like to move in with him. She says yes to both, and the happy pair leave the island together. Don't mess it up, dude!
